belay.P1: Stance is at the top of the slabby corner, above the small roofs, on a two-bolt anchor.
belay.P2: The station sits inside a stemming box at the end of the undercling traverse, on two bolts set offset from each other.
belay.P4: Belay on a ledge at the top of the pitch, on a two-bolt anchor.
belay.P6: The station is a lone bolt at the top of the headwall, backed up with a small cam, on the West Ridge.

belay.1: Belay by a small rotting tree once the bouldery start gives way to easier ground.
belay.3: Finish on Launch Ledge above the dihedral and short slab, then shift the belay roughly thirty feet left before the Scoop pitch.
belay.4: The station is a ledge at the top of the hand-crack finish above the giant scooped corner.
belay.5: Belay on a ledge reached by moving out and left around the small roof.
belay.6: The last technical stance is a ledge with a tree for the anchor.

belay.P1: Belay from a ledge at the top of the corner, anchored on two bolts.
belay.P2: The station is a ledge after the leftward traverse and corner, with a two-bolt anchor.
belay.P3: Stance is the Sky Lounge, a ledge at the top of the corner, on two bolts.
belay.P4: Belay in an alcove at the top of the crux pitch, on a two-bolt anchor that is the last point from which you can rappel.
belay.P5: Build the anchor from gear in a sandy alcove at the end of the crack.

belay.2: Belay on a very large ledge at the top of the hand crack, on the right side of the crest.
belay.3: The station is a good ledge above the roof pulls through the black band.
belay.4: Stop on a sloping ledge, using a fixed pin plus gear in a seam.
belay.6: Stance is on an easy slab at the top of the pitch.

belay.1: The station is a ledge at the top of the narrowing crack, equipped with bolts.
belay.2: Belay on a ledge above the bulge, with a three-bolt anchor.
belay.3: Stance is a ledge reached over the two small bulges, anchored on two bolts.
